name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. content.content:
# fix1-pool: review2 findings HP-1, HP-3 and HP-4 (HandlePool)

File edited: `formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` only. `Ern/Corpus/Lib.lean` and `Ern/Corpus/LibRunner.lean`
were not touched, because nothing in them referred to the renamed names. The pool operations
(`newPool`, `allocSlot`, `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `unresolve`, `freeSlot`) are unchanged, and so are the
ghost invariants `PoolWF`, `NoStale` and `CompExcl` and every proof except the renamings below.
Pre-existing uncommitted edits by another fixer (`contentEnd_preserves`, KM-2) were kept as they were.

Checks:
- `lake build` of the whole project succeeds (28 jobs) with no warnings.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.Lib.HandlePool` prints `constants 604, theorems 221` and
  `outside propext, Quot.sound: #[]`.
- There is no sorry, admit, native_decide, axiom, noncomputable or set_option in the file.

## HP-1 (major): the literal guarantees are stated and refuted, and the proved versions are renamed as same-pool restrictions

Spec passages (contract, HandlePool v0.4 annex = Annex D of `ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`):
- D.4 (3): "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné".
- D.3: "aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres. En particulier, aucune
  descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée".
- D.2: "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du
  pool".
- Brief obligation 5: "transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active
  companion descendant".

### Literal statements (new definitions)

- `FreeGuarantee` (HandlePool.lean:1445) is D.4 (3) as written. Its quantifier ranges over every ghost
  companion `r ∈ L.res`, with no `r.pool = pl.id`, and over every active **strict** descendant `x`
  (`r.comp ∈ ancs x`). Strict is the weaker reading of "descendante". The refutation uses a strict
  descendant, so it also refutes the reading that includes the companion itself.
- `PoolInv` (:1465) is `EntriesDisjoint ∧ NoStale ∧ FreeGuarantee`, as D.4 and the brief state it.
- `ModifyExclusive` (:1541) is D.2 as written. Take an active `Modify` companion `r₁` of a pool `pl`. Any
  active companion `r₂`, of any pool, whose footprint meets a leaf of `pl.storage` must be `r₁`. The
  refutation's second companion covers the **whole** storage (`afp 9 = footprint storage`). It is
  created by a `resolve` that is accepted while the `Modify` companion is already active. So the
  statement is refuted under every reading: "meets a leaf" or "covers all of the storage", state form or
  transition form ("bloque les nouvelles compagnes").

### Refutations (namespace `Witness`, new nested-pool run `nst`, `n0`–`n10`, contract `K0`)

The run is the reviewer's x10, with the states renamed. Pool 0 has storage 0 and `internal` 5. It is
resolved in `Modify` (companion 6, entry 7), and entry 7 is then released by a kernel `release`. A
kernel `derive(6, [1, 2], Modify)` gives authority 8, which is stored in place 4. `newPool(0, 8)` creates
pool 1 over the same storage, and `allocSlot(1, 6)` follows. `n10_reach : PReachI K0 nst n10` is proved,
and every step starts from a `KInv` state, decided through `Arena.KInvB`.

- `Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false` (:2156) proves
  `PReachI K0 nst n10 ∧ KInv n10.kern ∧ ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 n10 ∧ n10.pools[1]? = some plB10 ∧
  Exempt n10.kern plB10.internal 6`. `freeSlot(⟨1,0,0⟩)` of pool 1 is accepted on place 1, while
  companion 6 of pool 0 and its active descendant 8 cover place 1.
- `Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false` (:2168) proves `PReachI K0 nst n10 ∧ ¬ PoolInv K0 n10`.
- `Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false` (:2177) proves that the `Modify` companion 6 of pool 0
  is recorded and active in `n10`. `resolve(1, ⟨1,0,0⟩, Modify)` from `n10` is accepted. The reached
  state is `PReachI`, satisfies `¬ ModifyExclusive`, and has `afp 9 = footprint storage`.

### Proved versions, renamed as same-pool restrictions

The statements and proofs are unchanged. Each docstring now says that it states the same-pool
restriction, not the contract's statement, and points to the refutation.
- `FreeGuarantee` is now `FreeGuaranteeSamePool` (:1455). The docstring notes that it is weaker
  (same pool only) and stronger (it also covers the companion itself).
- `PoolInv` → `PoolInvSamePool` (:1471).
- `freeGuarantee_of` → `freeGuaranteeSamePool_of` (:1487).
- `pool_inv_preserved` → `pool_inv_preserved_same_pool` (:1510).
- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` → `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool` (:1531).
- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` → `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool` (:1552).
- The `CompExcl` docstring (:966) now says that it is the same-pool restriction of the D.2 sentence.
- `pool_entries_disjoint` and `pool_no_stale_access` keep their names and statements, which are D.4 items
  1 and 2 as written. Only their proof term now cites `pool_inv_preserved_same_pool`.

No other module used the old names. `grep` over `formal/` found none.

### Contract defect (record)

D.3 contradicts itself, and D.3's precondition contradicts D.4 (3), on nested pools. D.3 exempts
"`internal` et ses ancêtres". When the `internal` of pool B is derived from a companion of pool A, that
companion is an ancestor of B's `internal`. It is therefore exempt for `freeSlot` on B. The model
follows the precondition (`ContentEndPre`, `Exempt`), as the task requires. So `freeSlot` succeeds while
an active descendant of a companion covers the slot. That descendant is B's `internal` itself, and it
is active and covers the slot. This contradicts D.3 "En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une
compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée", D.4 (3), and the brief's transition guarantee.

D.2's sentence fails for the same reason. B's companion descends from A's `Modify` companion, so the
kernel accepts its derivation, and a new `Modify` companion is created over A's whole storage.

Two readings of the D.2 sentence exist. If "nouvelles compagnes" means only new companions of the
same pool, then `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool` is the statement. Under the wording as
written, which `ModifyExclusive` formalizes, the sentence is false. This needs arbitration. Brief
obligation 5 ("PoolInv = … + transition guarantee", theorem `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`) therefore
cannot be discharged as stated. It is a contract (specification-side) defect, not a module defect.

Possible repairs, which are not chosen here:
- (a) restrict the exemption to `internal` and the ancestors that are not companions of a live
  pool or their descendants;
- (b) restrict D.4 (3) and D.2 to the slot's pool;
- (c) forbid `newPool` with an `internal` that descends from a live companion.

Each of these changes accepted programs. For example, (a) and (c) reject the `freeSlot` or the
`newPool` of `n10`.

## HP-3 (minor, record only, no code change)

When a pool is dead (its `internal` is inactive, for example after a kernel `release` of `internal`),
its registry entry is kept. `HandleOK` still holds for its handles, and `ResolveRight` (which contains
`Active internal`) is checked first. So `resolve` on that pool gives `reject`, and `reject` is the only
outcome. The reviewer's evidence is `DeadPool.dead_pool_rejects` in `review2/libs/misc.lean`.

§89 says "a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure", and by §58 defined failure is
`fail`. D.1 says "détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle". No
recorded reading covers this case. H-R3 orders the right before handle validity, H-R3's alternative
gives the same verdict here, and H-R4 covers only a missing index. `pool_resolve_stale_fails` cites §89
but assumes `ResolveRight`, which excludes this case. This is recorded as a reading gap that needs
arbitration:
- (a) keep `reject`;
- (b) treat a dead pool's handle as a stale identity, which gives `fail`.

The example whose verdict changes is `resolve(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩, Observe)` on `wd` (`w4` after `release(3)`):
(a) gives `reject` and (b) gives `fail`. Nothing changed in code.

## HP-4 (minor, record only, no code change)

`freeSlot` is a transition outside O1–O16 (`XStep.contentEnd`). On a `PReachI` state whose slot content
is `Init`, `freeSlot` ends that content. Kernel `endUse` is rejected both for the slot place and for the
storage root, and `internal` stays active. The reviewer's evidence is
`FreeNotKernel.free_outside_kernel` in `review2/libs/misc.lean`. The library run's kernel side
therefore leaves kernel `Reachable`.

This conflicts with §36 ("These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel") and §89
("do not modify the authority-discipline kernel"). Yet the behaviour is prescribed by D.3 (the exemption
of `internal` and its ancestors in the end-of-use checks) and by brief obligation 5 ("freeSlot ends the
entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors"). This is a
**brief/contract-versus-spec contradiction** (§36 and §89 against D.3 and obligation 5). It is recorded,
not resolved: the task forbids changing the pool operations, and the charter hierarchy says such
contradictions are reported. The existing `Witness.freeSlot_not_endUse` (on `w4`) shows only an
`Uninit` slot. The `Init` case is the reviewer's `free_outside_kernel`, which was not imported into the
module.

## Not done

- The nested-pool case was not added to the corpus (`Corpus/Lib.lean`) because the corpus encodes
  cases from their sources with expected verdicts, and this case has no source verdict. The witness
  lives in `HandlePool.Witness`, next to the other contract-problem witnesses.
- `readings/handlepool.md` and `reports/handlepool.md` were not edited, because they are outside the
  allowed files. Their entries on `pool_inv_preserved`, `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` and
  `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` now refer to the `_same_pool` names. The contract defect above should
  be added to the readings as a new entry that needs arbitration.

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

4:Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.
11:5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
13:7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified. No case is corrected or bypassed.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F
cd /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean $F
rm -f $F

import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.EndFree

/-!
# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (items
D.1–D.4), which `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` does not define (§75, Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are
§36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the administering value; `writeShared` alone is
insufficient), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities), §38 and §46 (library state outside
`S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the guard over all registries of live administrations)
and §58 (outcomes, statics before `fail`).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57); `pstep_kernel` states what
every pool step is on the kernel side.
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool

open Ern.MemoryModel
open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §38, §46) -/

/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`;
non-normative library contract; §38, §46). -/
structure Slot where
  place : Nat
  gen : Nat
  live : Bool
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
structure Pool where
  id : Nat
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  slots : List Slot
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §37, §89;
non-normative library contract). -/
structure Handle where
  id : Nat
  slot : Nat
  gen : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary information creating no
right, §38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities
tagged with their slot and resolved generation. Read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. -/
structure Res where
  pool : Nat
  internal : Nat
  comp : Nat
  mode : Mode
  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Library state (§38, §46; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library contract): the
kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost
resolutions. -/
structure PState where
  kern : S3
  pools : List Pool
  nId : Nat
  res : List Res

/-- Initial library state (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): the initial kernel state, an empty
registry. -/
def PState.init (statics : Statics) : PState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩

/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩

/-- Administrative right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library
contract; §46). -/
def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0

/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
contract; §46). -/
def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }

/-! ## `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56) -/

/-- The pool registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
non-normative library contract): the `internal` identities of its live pools. -/
def liveInternals (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) : List Nat :=
  (pools.filter fun pl => decide (s.Active pl.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newPool(storage, internal)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative
library contract; §56, §76). -/
structure NewPoolPre (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.1: "reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena`" (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5). -/
  base : Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- D.1: every leaf of the input storage is `Uninit`. -/
  uninit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit
  /-- D.1, §56: `internal` is absent from the pool registry and from every other registry of live
  administrations `others`. -/
  guard : Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewPoolPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56, §76). -/
instance (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewPoolPre s pools others storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit) ∧
    Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library contract): a pool with
the fresh identity `nId`, one free slot of generation zero per child of the storage, the kernel
state unchanged (§46, §76). -/
def newPoolEff (L : PState) (storage internal : Nat) : PState :=
  { L with
    pools := L.pools ++ [⟨L.nId, storage, internal,
      (kids L.kern.P storage).map fun q => ⟨q, 0, false⟩⟩]
    nId := L.nId + 1 }

/-- `newPool` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §58; non-normative library contract):
`ok` or `reject`; `others` are the other registries of live administrations (§56). -/
def NewPoolStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (L : PState) :
    Outcome3 PState → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewPoolPre L.kern L.pools others storage internal) (newPoolEff L storage internal)

/-! ## `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot(pool, dst)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
non-normative library contract). "Apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" names no state
component and is not represented. -/
structure AllocSlotStatic (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.3, §36: live pool and `MetaRight`. -/
  right : AdminRight s pl
  /-- D.3: `dst` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- D.3: `dst` is a leaf (the handle is written into "la seule feuille `dst`"). -/
  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
  /-- D.3 with §67.1: the write of the handle needs exercisable `Modify` over `dst`. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- D.3: `dst` is not `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : s.I dst ≠ .init
  /-- D.3: `dst` holds no active authority. -/
  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True

/-- Decidability of `AllocSlotStatic` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §36, §67). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (AllocSlotStatic s pl dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (AdminRight s pl ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧ ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative
library contract): the slot becomes live with its generation kept; the handle is written into the
leaf `dst`, which alone becomes `Init` (§67 effect). -/
def allocSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PState :=
  { L with
    kern := write3Eff L.kern [dst]
    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) }

/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` for slot `i` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative
library contract; §37, §89). -/
def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩

/-- `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §58; non-normative library
contract): `reject` without the pool or a static precondition; then `fail` when no slot is free;
`ok` on any free slot. -/
inductive AllocSlotStep (j dst : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
  | static {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, sl.live = true) → AllocSlotStep j dst L .fail
  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      pl.slots[i]? = some sl → sl.live = false →
      AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok (allocSlotEff L j pl i sl dst))

/-! ## `resolve`, `resolveMany` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2) -/

/-- The handle designates a live slot of the pool at its generation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2,
D.3; §89; non-normative library contract); a slot index outside the pool designates nothing. -/
def HandleOK (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False

/-- Decidability of `HandleOK` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §89). -/
instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK pl h) := by
  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance

/-- Legal exercise of `internal` at mode `m` for the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2;
non-normative library contract): the preconditions of the `derive` of the companion from
`internal` over all leaves of the storage (§60). -/
def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  DerivePre s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m

/-- Decidability of `ResolveRight` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance

/-- State after the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60 effect; non-normative library
contract): authority `|A|`, derived from `internal` at mode `m` over all leaves of the storage. -/
def compS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  deriveEff s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m

/-- Observe derivations from `c`, one per region in order (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
`resolveMany` in `Observe`; §60; non-normative library contract): each accepted in the state left
by the previous ones. -/
def DerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → Prop
  | [] => True
  | r :: rs => DerivePre s c r .observe ∧ DerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs

/-- Decidability of `DerivesPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, §60). -/
instance decDerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) :
    (rs : List (List Nat)) → Decidable (DerivesPre s c rs)
  | [] => isTrue trivial
  | r :: rs =>
    have := decDerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Effect of the `Observe` derivations from `c`, in order (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60 effect).
-/
def derivesEff (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → S3
  | [] => s
  | r :: rs => derivesEff (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs

/-- Entry authorities of a batch from the companion `c` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative
library contract): `split` (§61) in `Modify`, successive `Observe` derivations (§60) in
`Observe`. -/
def EntriesPre (k : K) : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → Prop
  | .modify, s, c, rs => SplitPre k s c rs
  | .observe, s, c, rs => DerivesPre s c rs

/-- Decidability of `EntriesPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60, §61). -/
instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (m : Mode) (s : S3) (c : Nat)
    (rs : List (List Nat)) : Decidable (EntriesPre k m s c rs) := by
  cases m <;> unfold EntriesPre <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of the entry authorities of a batch (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60, §61 effects). -/
def entriesEff : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → S3
  | .modify, s, c, rs => splitEff s c rs
  | .observe, s, c, rs => derivesEff s c rs

/-- Regions of the entries designated by a batch: the footprint of each slot (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.2; non-normative library contract; §60). -/
def entryRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)

/-- Ghost entries of a batch: the `n`-th entry authority is `c + 1 + n`, for slot and generation of
the `n`-th handle (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary, §38). -/
def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs

/-- `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative
library contract): `reject` without the pool or the legal exercise of `internal`; then `fail` for
a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then the companion and the entry authority
derived from it, `reject` when the second derivation is not accepted. -/
inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })

/-- Validity of a batch (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library contract): every handle
designates a live slot at its generation; pairwise distinct slots in `Modify` only (§58, §89). -/
def BatchOK (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK pl h) ∧ (m = .modify → (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup)

/-- Decidability of `BatchOK` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58, §89). -/
instance (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Decidable (BatchOK pl hs m) := by
  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance

/-- `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative
library contract): `reject` without the pool or the legal exercise of `internal`; then an atomic
`fail` for an invalid batch; then one companion and the entry authorities (`EntriesPre`), `reject`
when they are not accepted. -/
inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) :
    Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ BatchOK pl hs m →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .fail
  | noEntries {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → BatchOK pl hs m →
      ¬ EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → BatchOK pl hs m →
      EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok { L with
        kern := entriesEff m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs)
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          batchEntries L.kern.A.length hs⟩] })

/-! ## `unresolve` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2) -/

/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (§62); `none` as soon as one release is not
accepted (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "Les règles de `release` … restent applicables"). -/
def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
  | s, [] => some s
  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none

/-- The resolution of companion `c` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; ghost lookup, §38). -/
def findRes (L : PState) (c : Nat) : Option Res := L.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c

/-- Authorities released by `unresolve` of `r` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library
contract): the entry authorities still active, then the companion (§62). -/
def unresolveList (s : S3) (r : Res) : List Nat :=
  ((r.entries.map (·.1)).filter fun a => decide (s.Active a)) ++ [r.comp]

/-- `unresolve(c)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative library
contract): the releases of `unresolveList`; `reject` when one is not accepted or `c` is no
companion. -/
inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | none : findRes L c = none → UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | reject {r : Res} : findRes L c = some r → releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = none →
      UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes L c = some r →
      releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = some s' →
      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3) -/

/-- `x` is exempt from the end-of-use checks of a slot of the pool of `internal` `i`: `internal` or
one of its ancestors (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; non-normative
library contract; §69). -/
def Exempt (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Prop := x = i ∨ x ∈ s.ancs i

/-- Decidability of `Exempt` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Decidable (Exempt s i x) := by unfold Exempt; infer_instance

/-- §69.2 for storage that dies with the content (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the end-of-use
effects of O12; non-normative library contract): an active derived authority over a leaf of a place
that stops being usable is held within the slot `q` or by a dying holder. -/
def DyingAccessOK (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l) →
      heldIn s.P q y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `DyingAccessOK` (§69.2). -/
instance (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Decidable (DyingAccessOK s q j) := by
  unfold DyingAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- §69.3 with the exemption of D.3 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract):
anchor `x` of a place remaining usable is not held within the slot `q` and keeps a live holder;
unless exempt, it is not a root of `q`. -/
def ContentAnchorOK (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P q y.holder ∧ (¬ Exempt s i x → ¬ IsRootOf s q y) ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `ContentAnchorOK` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Decidable (ContentAnchorOK s q i x) := by
  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of the end of the content of slot place `q` of the pool of `internal` `i`
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible"; the preconditions
of O12, §69, excluding `internal` and its ancestors; non-normative library contract). §69.1 is not
a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives it from `AdminRight`. -/
structure ContentEndPre (k : K) (s : S3) (q i : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.3: no active authority covers the entry except `internal` and its ancestors (§69.2 on the
  leaves of the entry, with the exemption). -/
  entry : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j → (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) →
    Exempt s i j
  /-- §69.2 on the storage that dies with the content. -/
  dying : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j
  /-- D.3, §69.3: no usable dependency is invalidated. -/
  anchors : ∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x
  /-- D.3, §69.4: no ending leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (q i : Nat) :
    Decidable (ContentEndPre k s q i) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j →
      (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) → Exempt s i j) ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j) ∧
    (∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
contract): the effects of O12 on the slot content (`endUseEff`, §69), no deallocation; the slot
becomes free and its generation is incremented. -/
def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
  { L with
    kern := endUseEff L.kern sl.place
    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }

/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36; §58;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool, without a live pool or `MetaRight`;
then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then `reject` unless the end of
the content is admissible (`ContentEndPre`). -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .fail
  | noEnd {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex; §38, §46, §57) -/

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
operation (§57, §58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :
      NewPoolStep others st i L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | allocSlot {L L' : PState} {j dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolve {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolveMany {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | unresolve {L L' : PState} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | freeSlot {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
      PStep k L L'

/-- Library states reachable from the initial library state (§47) by library steps (HandlePool v0.4
annex; non-normative library contract). -/
inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReach k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReach k statics L → PStep k L L' → PReach k statics L'

/-- Library runs in which every step starts from a kernel state satisfying `KInv` (§57; HandlePool
v0.4 annex). Under the guarantee of §57 every library-reachable state is such a state
(`PReach.toI`); the pool theorems are stated on these runs, so that they do not depend on that
guarantee. -/
inductive PReachI (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReachI k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReachI k statics L → KInv L.kern → PStep k L L' →
      PReachI k statics L'

/-- Kernel side of library runs (§57, §69 effect; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): a kernel step
O1–O16, or the end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` for some `internal`
`i`. -/
inductive XStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | kernel {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' → XStep k s s'
  | contentEnd {s : S3} {q i : Nat} : ContentEndPre k s q i → XStep k s (endUseEff s q)

/-- States reachable from `S3.init statics` by `XStep` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
inductive XReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  | init : XReach k statics (S3.init statics)

/-! ## `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4) -/

/-- `PoolInv`, item 1 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library contract): the entries of
every pool lie in its storage and are pairwise disjoint (§40). -/
def EntriesDisjoint (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ pl ∈ L.pools,
    (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sl.place, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) ∧
    ∀ (a b : Nat) (sa sb : Slot), pl.slots[a]? = some sa → pl.slots[b]? = some sb → a ≠ b →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sa.place, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sb.place

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex,
D.4: "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot
concerné"; non-normative library contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active strict
descendant of a companion covers the slot concerned (§43, §69). The contract does not restrict the
companion to the pool of the slot. This guarantee is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`): D.3 exempts "`internal` et ses ancêtres", which
may include a companion of another pool. -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- Same-pool restriction of the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3;
non-normative library contract). This is not the contract's statement (`FreeGuarantee`): only the
companions of the slot's pool are quantified (`r.pool = pl.id`). On that point it is weaker; it also
covers the companion itself, and on that point it is stronger (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuaranteeSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative
library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a companion of the pool
is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and
`ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuaranteeSamePool_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a
resolution of the pool, or an active descendant of it, covers the slot (§43, §69). This is not the
contract's statement: `FreeGuarantee` is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.2

/-- Exclusivity of a `Modify` companion, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
"Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool";
non-normative library contract): an active `Modify` companion of a pool is the only active
companion that covers a leaf of that pool's storage (§43, §50). The contract does not restrict the
other companions to the same pool. This property is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
def ModifyExclusive (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, ∀ pl ∈ L.pools, r₁.pool = pl.id → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify →
    (∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp r₂.comp, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) → r₁.comp = r₂.comp

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La
propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state
of a library run (`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is
the only active companion of that pool (§43, §50). This is not the contract's statement:
`ModifyExclusive`, which also covers the companions of other pools, is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

/-- Decidability of `ancestor` (§39). -/
instance (F : Frames) (f₁ f₂ : Nat) : Decidable (ancestor F f₁ f₂) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∈ _))

/-! ## Parent chains (§40, §42) -/

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along the link `org`, nearest first, within fuel `k` (§40 structural
parents, §42 origins). Only links to a smaller index are followed (§49, last paragraph). -/
def chainF (org : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | 0, _ => []
  | k + 1, i =>
    match org i with
    | some o => if o < i then o :: chainF org k o else []
    | none => []

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along `org` (§40, §42); fuel `i` suffices since the chain
decreases. -/
def chain (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chainF org i i

/-! ## Places, leaves, footprints (§40) -/

/-- Holder of an authority (§42) or owner of a place (§40): a frame or a place. -/
inductive Holder where
  | frame (f : Nat)
  | place (p : Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Logical place (§40): optional structural parent, owner, abstract `kind`. Its identity is its
index in `P`; its death marker is `S3.dead`. -/
structure Place where
  parent : Option Nat
  owner : Holder
  kind : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr
